description:
Decision needed: what map type should the workspace use for wire-format JSON object fields?

The workspace currently uses `std::collections::HashMap` for every wire-format map field across the type crates. Examples:
- `Email.mailbox_ids: HashMap<Id, bool>`
- `Email.keywords: HashMap<Keyword, bool>`
- `Email.body_values: HashMap<String, EmailBodyValue>`
- `Task.localizations: Option<HashMap<String, PatchObject>>` (canonical for JSCalendar/JSContact families)
- `CalendarEvent.localizations: Option<HashMap<String, PatchObject>>`
- `CalendarEvent.recurrence_overrides: Option<HashMap<String, PatchObject>>`
- `ContactCard.localizations: Option<HashMap<String, PatchObject>>`
- `ContactCard.address_book_ids: Option<HashMap<Id, bool>>`
- `ContactCard.members: Option<HashMap<String, bool>>`
- `ContactCard.keywords: Option<HashMap<String, bool>>` (after JMAP-glx8.3)
- All `*/set update` parameters in all client crates: `Option<HashMap<Id, PatchObject>>`
- `SetResponse.created/updated/notCreated/notUpdated/notDestroyed`
- `Request.createdIds` / `Response.createdIds`
- 40+ sites in 14+ crates

`HashMap` produces nondeterministic iteration order, and serde_json serializes a HashMap in iteration order. So wire-format output for any map field with N>1 entries is nondeterministic across runs / Rust versions / DefaultHasher seeds.

JSON object key order is not semantically significant per RFC 8259, so this is not a wire-format-correctness bug. But it does break:
1. Server cache/E-Tag/content-hash schemes that hash serialized wire bytes.
2. Snapshot/golden-file tests in downstream consumers.
3. HTTP-level diff tooling comparing JMAP request/response bodies across runs.

This bead asks: should the workspace adopt a wire-format-deterministic map type across all type crates, and if so, which one?

Options:
(a) Status quo — `HashMap` everywhere. Document the nondeterminism in workspace AGENTS.md and tell consumers "don't rely on key order."
(b) `BTreeMap` everywhere — alphabetical, deterministic, zero new dep. Loses insertion-order semantics (none of the JMAP wire types specify ordering, so this is fine). Minimum-change sweep.
(c) `indexmap::IndexMap` everywhere — preserves insertion order. Adds a workspace dependency. Matches what `serde_json::Map` does with `preserve_order` enabled.
(d) Enable the `preserve_order` feature on `serde_json` workspace-wide. Affects only fields typed as `serde_json::Value` / `serde_json::Map`; does not affect `HashMap` directly. Solves the localizations-via-Value pre-diff behavior but doesn't address the post-diff HashMap fields.

Trigger: JMAP-glx8.20 — `ContactCard.localizations` was migrated from `Option<serde_json::Value>` (where `serde_json::Map` defaults to BTreeMap order) to `Option<HashMap<String, PatchObject>>`, swapping deterministic alphabetical order for nondeterministic. The same field shape now lives in jmap-tasks-types::Task and jmap-calendars-types::CalendarEvent.

Recommendation: option (b) BTreeMap, on the grounds that:
- Minimum-change sweep (no new deps).
- Wire-format determinism without extra runtime overhead vs HashMap.
- Matches the pre-diff localizations behavior (`serde_json::Map` default).
- JMAP specs do not specify ordering, so alphabetical is as good as any.

Scope of the sweep if (b) lands:
- Canonical types: jmap-types methods.rs (SetResponse, Request, Response), jmap-mail-types email.rs, jmap-tasks-types task.rs, jmap-calendars-types event.rs, jmap-contacts-types card.rs, jmap-jscalendar-types lib.rs (recurrence_overrides).
- All sibling extension-types crates by the canonical-template rule.
- All client-crate /set update parameters (sealed by jmap-base-client trait? need to check).
- Tests using HashMap-literal constructors will need find-replace.

Scope of (a) (status quo + doc):
- Add a workspace AGENTS.md section explaining the nondeterminism is intentional.
- Update JMAP-glx8.20 with the policy decision.
- Update any downstream consumer docs.

Workspace consequences: option (b) is a public-API change for every type-crate that has not yet hit 1.0. None have, all still 0.1.x. So no semver-breaking-change drama, but every consumer needs to adjust their HashMap literals / type signatures.

The trigger bead JMAP-glx8.20 is blocked on this decision.
title: Workspace policy: wire-format map ordering for HashMap<_, _> fields
